# Reference 079 — Electrical Fields Generated by Blood Flow

## Source

Trivedi DP, Hallock KJ, Bergethon PR.

**Electric Fields Caused by Blood Flow Modulate Vascular Endothelial Electrophysiology and Nitric Oxide Production.**

Bioelectromagnetics. 2013;34(1):22–30.

PMCID: PMC3522793

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3522793/

## Relevance to the text

Blood is an electrically conductive ionic fluid.

Its movement through blood vessels produces an electrokinetic vascular streaming potential (EVSP).

Experimental in-vivo measurements cited in the paper report vascular streaming electric fields in the range of approximately 0.7–3.0 V/m.

The phenomenon arises from the movement of conductive fluid relative to the charged vascular wall.

Blood circulation therefore represents not only mechanical transport of matter but also a measurable electrodynamic process.
